name: The Reluctant Seal
setup: A precursor seal, intact, and the purpose-shadow on it reads PRISON rather than vault. It is not locked so much as decided. Probing it is permitted; opening it is a different question and a worse one.
hintTiers: The seam does not respond to force, pressure, or heat. It responded, once, to being addressed.
The shadow on it is not decoration — it is a label, and it was left by someone who expected to be read.
It can be opened. Everything about how it was made is an argument that it should not be.

party.ifYouBringPeople: ⛔ *THE PURPOSE-SHADOW READS PRISON RATHER THAN VAULT.* ⚠️ A party makes probing SAFER and opening WORSE — more people to catch a mistake, and more people present when a decided thing stops being decided. ⚑ It is not locked so much as decided, and a party can decide back at it.
party.whatItAsksOfAParty: ⛔ Whether you will stop. ⚑ The failure state is a party in which one member keeps probing after the others have understood.
party.foldNote: ⚠️ A folded PROTECT ally is what you want and will not be enough — ⛔ and the cell should say so before it is opened.

_partyClauseWhy: ⛔ THE PARTY CLAUSE — R36/R36a, authored 2026-09-05. Every encounter in the corpus was written when a fight was ONE PERSON AGAINST ONE OPPONENT. ⚑ R36 makes a party member fight from their own sheet; R36a caps three acting fully and folds the rest. ⚠️ THE CLAUSE IS ADDITIVE — no prose changed. It is what a GM reads when more than one person is present.
